watch: Nvidia CEO resignation impacts AI stocks; watch for permanent CEO announcement.
Hot October CPI suggests a December Fed hike; watch PPI and Fed speakers.

market.mood: Risk appetite is fragile: AI leadership is cracking under the Nvidia CEO's exit, hot inflation and a pending Fed hike, with the S&P 500 down about 0.3–0.4% on Thursday after Wednesday's 1.3% relief rally.

themes.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns, AI complex sells off
themes.what_happened: Nvidia said Huang is stepping down after a board probe into his personal relationships, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. NVDA fell sharply on Thursday (intraday reports range from about 5% to 10%), CoreWeave fell 13.6% a day after jumping 27%, and global AI stocks and Asian and European tech sold off.
themes.why_it_matters: Nvidia is the centerpiece of the AI build-out and is already down about 25% from its peak a month ago, so leadership uncertainty hits an AI trade that was already jittery over spending and returns.

our_exposure.why: Direct hit: CEO exit, probe and a sharp drop; earnings due Nov 17.
Fell about 5.8% Thursday, giving back part of Wednesday's 11.9% jump.
Down about 8.5% Thursday as storage and memory sold off with AI.
Eased about 5% Thursday with the AI storage and memory group.
AI infrastructure supplier; sensitive to any slowdown in AI capex sentiment.
Mega-cap tech weakness, but Alphabet is not Nvidia-dependent in the same way.

themes.next: Nvidia earnings are expected Nov 17. Watch for a permanent CEO announcement and the probe's findings, which could deepen the selloff if more serious.

themes.title: Hot October CPI puts a December Fed hike in play, 10-year back near 5%
themes.what_happened: October CPI rose 0.4% against 0.3% expected, and core rose 0.3% against 0.2% expected. The 2-year yield jumped about 18 bps to roughly 4.74% and the 10-year rose about 12 bps to roughly 5.0%. Markets now fully price a 25 bp December hike, with an 11–14% chance of 50 bp after Waller said a half-point move should be considered.
themes.why_it_matters: A higher rate path, not just higher yields, pressures long-duration tech multiples and the dollar-sensitive commodity complex.

our_exposure.why: Chips led the post-CPI slide; Nvidia hit its most oversold reading since 2019.
Memory names fell with chips on the rate-hike repricing.
High-multiple AI hardware is vulnerable to a higher rate path.
Hot CPI firmed the dollar; FCX fell about 3.2% on Nov 10.
Higher short rates help bank margins, but a hawkish Fed raises credit and market risk.
Higher short rates help bank margins, but a hawkish Fed raises credit and market risk.

themes.next: PPI is due Friday (Nov 13), with Fed speakers and the 30-year Treasury auction to follow. The December FOMC decision is the main event: 25 bp versus 50 bp.

themes.title: Democratic midterm sweep and data-center backlash hit AI power names
themes.what_happened: Democrats won both chambers of Congress. Texas voters elected a governor who campaigned on a data-center moratorium, and local data-center restrictions passed widely. Vistra fell about 14–15% on Nov 4, GE Vernova fell about 11.5% and Vertiv about 9%, and KeyBanc downgraded Vistra to Sector Weight.
themes.why_it_matters: Tighter data-center permitting and scrutiny could slow the AI power and infrastructure build-out, though analysts note signed contracts still stand and legislation would face hurdles.

our_exposure.why: Large Texas exposure; fell about 14% and was downgraded by KeyBanc.
Data-center equipment supplier; fell about 9% on the election.
Build-out risk, but existing hyperscaler data centers become more valuable.
Hyperscaler: slower overbuild risk versus tighter permitting; a Vistra PPA counterparty.

themes.next: Watch Texas moratorium and permitting actions, state utility commission decisions, and congressional hearings on the AI build-out. FERC rules on co-located data centers aren't expected until 1H 2027.

themes.title: Oil slides on Iran peace hopes, then whipsaws on Trump comments
themes.what_happened: Brent is around $92–94, with WTI around $87. Brent is down about 20% in November and WTI about 16%, after Trump signaled restraint on Iran. Prices bounced Thursday after Trump said no Iran deal is needed and Iran denied talks, while Hormuz shipping attacks continue.
themes.why_it_matters: Lower oil eases the inflation pressure behind the Fed's hawkish turn, but the Iran headlines are two-way and move crude several percent a day.

our_exposure.why: Brent down about 20% this month; small 1% position limits impact.
Lower energy and input costs would ease margin pressure.
Lower fuel and shipping costs; consumer spending support.

themes.next: Watch for any US-Iran negotiation news, further Hormuz tanker incidents, and Saudi and Iraqi output, which was at wartime or multi-year highs in October.

themes.title: Copper miners in a four-week retreat
themes.what_happened: The copper tracker CPER is about 9% below its September peak. Freeport-McMoRan fell 3.2% on Nov 10 to $60.31 after the CPI-driven dollar move, then bounced 3% on Nov 11 to $62.12. It is still about 22% below its Aug 25 high.
themes.why_it_matters: Copper miners are trading as a rate- and dollar-sensitive risk asset, so Fed-hike repricing is a headwind despite tight physical supply in China.

our_exposure.why: Down about 11% over 20 sessions; the Wednesday bounce is inside a downtrend.

themes.next: Watch the dollar and Treasury yields around PPI and the Fed. Also watch China physical copper tightness, where Yangshan premiums hit a record.
